description: Strong prevention governance links surveillance finance workforce community trust and access.
Technology expands while accountability access prevention and public health governance lag.
Climate health governance coordinates heat smoke flood water disease exposure and emergency planning.
Care systems lack workforce finance standards caregiver support and long-term institutional capacity.
Preparedness relies on surveillance labs supply chains communication social protection and coordination.
Community care crisis alternatives school support and trauma-informed systems require stronger governance.
Health governance integrates prevention care public health technology accountability climate readiness and justice.
Weak finance workforce monitoring participation and care capacity produce public health fragility.
